mechanism: Give the true thirty unit boundary edges and ten actual internal gray-grid interfaces the same red style. The forty highlighted unit segments invite counting subdivision edges in the gray perimeter: 240/40=6 and 30*6^2=1080 (C), although the original fill still distinguishes exterior from interior. Every mark is an existing grid edge with a specified boundary-class role.
mathematical_solution: Enumerate unit edges of the gray cells by exact frozen endpoints: 30 have gray incidence one and are perimeter; all gray-gray interfaces have incidence two and are interior. Thus the given 240 cm equals 30 side units, side=8 cm. The big 6x5 rectangle area is 30*8^2=1920 cm^2, uniquely D. Colors cannot change cell incidence or gray area. The source already explicitly contains all thirty grid squares; recoloring their existing boundaries adds no partition or given.
